claim: A command of 64 or more (kCmdNumberic) is not an instruction but the number command - 64, and the channel decides its meaning: on channel 1 it sets the level's secret total, on 2 it credits a secret, on 3 it shows level message n (and on 6, modern maps only, ends to level n). 325 such commands appear in all 43 campaign maps.
evidence: NBlood/source/blood/src/eventq.cpp:375-398 (the rxId switch); eventq.h:27-32 the channel numbers
recount 2026-11-26 over the 43 campaign maps: 325 objects carry a command of 64 or more, in all 43 maps; 227 send on channel 2, 55 on 3, 42 on 1 and one on user channel 165
use: Read a command with its channel: bloodmap.blood_types.classify('command', n) names kCmdNumberic + value and RESERVED_CHANNELS names the channel. A secret is tx 2 with 64+n, a total tx 1 with 64+n.

checked.how: eventq.cpp:375-398 read in evSend (from :352): kChannelTextOver -> trTextOver(cmd-64), kChannelModernEndLevelCustom under NOONE_EXTENSIONS -> levelEndLevelCustom(cmd-64), kChannelSetTotalSecrets -> levelSetupSecret, kChannelSecretFound -> levelTriggerSecret; eventq.h:27-32 channels 1,2,3,6; kCmdNumberic 64 at eventq.h:124. Recounted with knowledge/blood/findings/probes/audit2_numeric_commands.py: 325 objects in 43 of 43 maps; channel 2 227, 3 55, 1 42, 165 1.
